title: Allowable Load for an Offset Overhead Process-Equipment Hanger

summary: An allowable-load bending problem integrating load paths, internal resultants, unsymmetric composite-section properties, the parallel-axis theorem, section modulus, and engineering assessment.
textbookChapters: Moments of inertia for an area
idealizedImageAlt: Instructor reference idealization of an offset overhead hanger with fixed support D, suspended load P at E, horizontal offset L, bend radius R, critical section a-a, and an unsymmetric flanged section defined by B, H, t1, and t2.
problemStatement:
A process plant uses an offset steel hanger to support a suspended valve or maintenance fixture while clearing nearby piping and equipment. The chain applies a vertical load P at E, and the hanger transfers that load to the overhead structure through the fixed connection at D.

Evaluate the hanger at section a-a. For the assigned section, model the top flange as B by t2, the web as t1 by (H - 2t2), and the bottom flange as (t1 + 2t2) by t2. These are three nonoverlapping rectangles.
engineeringGoal: Determine the maximum allowable suspended load such that the largest flexural normal-stress magnitude at section a-a does not exceed the specified allowable bending stress. Identify the governing extreme fiber and explain which geometry changes most directly increase capacity.
